finding: The 2021 report described a laboratory-related incident as extremely unlikely although the study had limited access to records and sites; the project assesses that this confidence exceeded what the investigation could justify.
actor_response: WHO's director-general said on publication day that the laboratory assessment was not extensive enough; WHO stated in August 2021 that evidence was insufficient to rule out any hypothesis (S03, S05). No account of how the ranking was approved was found.
corrective_action_requested: WHO to document how the ranking language was selected and approved and the evidence standard applied (D.4.4; proposals/who-accountability-requests.md, request 2).

finding: The director-general publicly challenged the adequacy of the joint report's laboratory assessment on the day of publication and criticised premature downplaying in July 2021, disclosing disagreement rather than presenting a single institutional voice.
corrective_action_requested: None for this control; how the objection was recorded and answered is covered by the request under F01.

finding: WHO published later qualifications and assessments in 2021, 2025 and 2026, but the project has not established whether the historical 2021 report carries a prominent note directing readers to them; under the boundary test the operation of this control is not evidenced (regraded from opportunity for improvement, 17 November 2026).
corrective_action_requested: Attach a dated contextual note to the 2021 report, leaving it unaltered, that states WHO's subsequent position and links to later assessments (proposals/who-accountability-requests.md, request 1).

finding: SAGO's 2025 assessment stated that the laboratory-related hypothesis could not be evaluated because requested information was not provided, distinguishing unavailable evidence from evidence against that hypothesis.
corrective_action_requested: None for this control; a dated register of the outstanding requests (D.1.3) would strengthen it (proposals/who-accountability-requests.md, request 4).

finding: WHO stated in March 2023 that market-sample data could and should have been shared three years earlier, and in June 2025 reported that requested early sequences, market-animal information and laboratory information had still not been shared.
corrective_action_requested: Publish an itemised inventory of requested data still withheld, with reasons and a release timetable, protecting legitimate patient privacy.

finding: SAGO reported that it had no access to verify conditions at the Wuhan Institute of Virology or the Wuhan CDC laboratory and that its requests for information were refused.
corrective_action_requested: Permit independently verifiable access to the requested records and sites, stating any legitimate limits on that access.

finding: HHS found that WIV repeatedly failed to supply the original laboratory notebooks and electronic files NIH requested to assess a grant-compliance question, treating this as an aggravating factor in a ten-year debarment; the inspector general records that WIV had cooperated with monitoring for several years before the outbreak.
actor_response: WIV did not contest the determination (S14).
corrective_action_requested: Produce the requested original records for an independent compliance review.

finding: The HHS inspector general found that EcoHealth did not effectively monitor its subaward and could not obtain WIV documentation requested in oversight, alongside reporting and financial deficiencies.
actor_response: EcoHealth disputed important points of the audit, including report timing (S13).
corrective_action_requested: Publish a point-by-point account of upheld and disputed findings with supporting records, and explain how access to subrecipient records was enforced and what happened when it failed.

finding: The HHS inspector general found that NIH did not effectively monitor the awards and subawards and did not follow up a late progress report for nearly two years.
actor_response: NIH concurred or generally concurred with the recommendations (S13).
corrective_action_requested: Clarify escalation rules for late reports and unexpected outcomes under awards, and demonstrate timely monitoring.

finding: NIH concurred or generally concurred with the inspector general's recommendations; the project did not find recommendation-by-recommendation reporting of their implementation.
actor_response: Concurrence recorded in the audit report (S13).
corrective_action_requested: Report implementation of each recommendation with dated evidence.
status: control partly operating; implementation not evidenced

finding: The inspector general published an independent audit of award monitoring that set out its findings, the auditees' responses and EcoHealth's disagreements, and stated that it did not assess scientific results or pandemic causation. Assessed part (D.5.3 partly applies to audit bodies): publication of the audit with the auditees' responses and its stated limits; whether the inspector general's own work is externally reviewed was not assessed.
corrective_action_requested: none

finding: Relationships relevant to his origins-related contributions in The Lancet were not fully disclosed at first and were expanded in a June 2021 addendum. Recorded as an observation because the actor is an individual author (grading rule 7; regraded from minor nonconformity, 17 November 2026); the journal's review of disclosures is graded under F13.
actor_response: Updated disclosure statement published in the addendum (S18).
corrective_action_requested: none (individual author; disclosure already updated)

finding: The journal published the expanded disclosure as an addendum, but the project has found no account of why its initial disclosure review was insufficient or how relevant relationships are now reviewed.
actor_response: Addendum published June 2021 (S18); no explanation of the review process found.
corrective_action_requested: Explain how disclosures are now reviewed where authors have institutional, research or funding relationships relevant to the subject.

finding: An advocacy group requested editorial action on Proximal Origin in July 2023; the project has not yet searched journal records for a substantive editorial response, so the operation of this control is not evidenced.
corrective_action_requested: Publish a reasoned editorial account of substantive criticisms and relevant correspondence, whatever its conclusion.

finding: The paper argued against laboratory-based scenarios while acknowledging that some explanations could not be proved or disproved; published accounts of the authors' private messages are disputed, and whether the published confidence matched the authors' contemporaneous assessments has not been adjudicated here. Recorded as an observation because the actors are individual authors (grading rule 7; regraded from not evidenced, 17 November 2026); the journal's handling is graded under F14.
actor_response: Andersen publicly rejected Public's interpretation of the messages (S21).
corrective_action_requested: Suggestion, not a corrective-action request: a contextual chronology of how the authors' assessments changed and which evidence drove the changes, linked to complete relevant exchanges, would help readers; any such request belongs with the journal's own correspondence process.

finding: The 11 July 2023 release, which establishes that Slack excerpts were public by that date, links one report file while a near-identical file with the same title and date is also hosted, and the project has found no account of the differences.
corrective_action_requested: State which file is authoritative and what differs between them.

finding: Public described its July 2023 release as the full cache and linked Slack and email files of 47 MB and 184 MB; the description establishes what the publisher released, not the completeness of the communications.
corrective_action_requested: State the source and scope of the collection and publish integrity data for the files.

finding: The 22 July 2026 announcement describes its documents as newly released. The project's comparison on 17 November 2026 found that the main file covers 30 April 2020 to 28 June 2023 and that, apart from two messages on 30 April 2020, none of its messages appear in the two July 2023 collections, so the novelty claim is consistent with the evidence checked.
corrective_action_requested: None. Suggestion: state the date range covered and why Bates pages SLACK_000001 to SLACK_000215 are not included.
status: closed (project comparison complete; limits in research/slack-release-provenance.md)

finding: The September 2023 WIV debarment determination and the January 2025 EcoHealth and Daszak debarment notices are HHS-letterhead documents, but the only copies the project located are hosted on the House committee majority's website; a bounded search on 17 November 2026 found no HHS or SAM.gov copy, and the SAM.gov exclusion search could not be fetched. The 2025 notices' text is undated, their date coming from the file names and the committee's release. Whether HHS publishes these decisions in a primary location is therefore not evidenced.
corrective_action_requested: State where HHS publishes its suspension and debarment determinations, or which official register records them, and provide or link a dated primary copy or exclusion record for each of the three decisions, with any later modification noted.
